title: Khwaja Shaik on the NACD keynote — 'We usually treat integrity as an ethics question. Eric reframes it as an architecture question'
summary: A board-level technology executive writes up the keynote for other directors and lands on the move that makes the argument work: integrity treated as a design property rather than a moral one. He retells the Sol Price arc — capped margins, a board that pushed him out, and the protégé who carried the principles into Costco — as the same leader with the same values and a different structure.
blockquote: We usually treat integrity as an ethics question. Eric reframes it as an architecture question. If your governance is designed only to maximize short-term value, financial gravity will eventually pull your mission down, whatever your values statement says.
